newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada energy group sees high reserve replacement.
newsitem.headline: Canada energy group sees high reserve replacement.

text.p: The Canadian Association of Petroleum Producers said on Tuesday that brisk drilling activity in western Canada led to improved oil and gas reserve relacement in 1995.

"Industry's commitment to the western sedimentary basin is demonstrated by high levels of drilling and investment over the last two years and into 1996," CAPP chairman Dennis Sharp, who is also chief executive of CS Resources Ltd, said in a statement announcing the association's annual Canadian reserve report.
CAPP said Canadian crude oil reserves in conventional areas totalled 3.7 million barrels at the end of 1995, nearly unchanged from the previous year.
It said Alberta, Canada's largest producing province, replaced 72 percent of its 1995 oil production, up from 54 percent in 1994.
Alberta's crude reserves fell 3.7 percent from to 2.48 billion barrels from the year-earlier 2.58 billion.
Saskatchewan additions replaced 172 percent of 1995 oil output, translating into a 9.5 percent increase in its remaining reserves, CAPP said.
In natural gas, Canadian reserve additions replaced about 120 percent of 1995 production after three years of high gas drilling levels, it said.
Gas reserves in the country totalled 68.5 trillion cubic feet, 1.6 percent above the 1994 estimate of 67.4 TCF.
In Alberta, 116 percent of production was replaced.
British Columbia's 1995 year-end reserves jumped 4.7 percent to 9.0 TCF, CAPP said.
The association, which represents 180 Canadian exploration and production companies, said developed synthetic crude oil reserves increased by 614 million barrels to 2.57 million.
CAPP said it recently changed its method of reporting synthetic oil reserves by using numbers provided by project operators, which resulted in the rise.
Developed bitumen reserves jumped by 175 million barrels in 1995 to 1.24 million barrels, it said.
